source: Nacherzaehlt nach dem Philogelos ("Der Lachfreund", Hierokles und Philagrios, vermutlich 4./5. Jh. n. Chr.; Zaehlung nach Thierfelder 1968, Nr. 1-265). Nur die Witze mit einer Nummer im Feld "philogelos" sind dort belegt (Stand 19.11.2026, geprueft gegen den griechischen Text bei eulogikon.org, Nr. 1-191). Die uebrigen Witze sind freie Erfindungen im Stil des Philogelos und duerfen nicht als antik ausgegeben werden. Der griechische Text liegt noch nicht im Repo.
note: Die Hauptfigur vieler Witze ist der Scholastikos (Gelehrter, Pedant, Student). Kurz halten: Ein Scherben bietet Platz fuer etwa 3 Zeilen zu je 20 Zeichen.

jokes.en:
A scholar nearly drowned.
He swore never to touch water again until he had learned to swim.

"I heard you were dead!"
"As you see, I am alive."
"But the man who told me is more reliable than you."

Patient: "Doctor, when I wake I'm dizzy for half an hour."
Doctor: "Then wake up half an hour later."

A scholar wanted to sell his house.
He carried a single brick around town as a sample.

Barber: "How shall I cut your hair?"
Customer: "In silence."

"Why do you never answer my letters?"
"I'd rather you didn't ask a man who is not at home."

A scholar dreamed he was at sea.
He slept with his feet out of the bed, so as not to get them wet.

A scholar was asked the hour.
"Come back when the sun is out," he said.

A scholar's friend coughed in the night.
"Stop it!" he said. "You'll wake the thief."

"Is that your brother or the one who looks like him?"
"Both," said the twin.

A bald man was given a comb as a gift.
"Thank you," he said. "I will keep it for my memories."

A miser heard that grain was cheap this year.
He hanged himself, because he had kept so much of his own.

"Why do you carry a lamp in broad daylight?"
"I'm looking for an honest man. And some oil."

"This wine has turned to vinegar."
"Good. Then it will last longer."

A scholar was warned the ship was leaking.
"Then I'll wait on the shore," he said, "and take the next one that's dry."

A scholar shouted into a well and heard his own voice.
"So there is someone down there," he said, "and he is rude."

Father: "What did you learn today?"
Son: "That you owe the teacher money."

A scholar bought a donkey that would not eat.
"It's a bargain," he said. "Think of the saving."

"I have an excellent memory."
"Then pay me what you owe."
"On second thought, I have forgotten that."

A scholar left his house on a cart to get fitter.
The horse did all the walking.
